description: Rick retraces a youthful journey from northern California down through Baja and mainland Mexico to the Yucatán, following migration, indigenous traditions, markets and regional cooking from San Francisco to the Caribbean.

s09e01.description: Rick begins in northern California, following San Francisco's food history and the Gold Rush-era Hangtown fry before setting the compass south toward Mexico.

s09e02.description: The California coast leads into Los Angeles, where old and new immigrant food meet around Olvera Street; farther south, a sea-urchin diver in San Diego supplies the makings of a fiery fish chilli.

s09e03.description: After classic diner steak and eggs, Rick crosses at Tijuana and reaches Ensenada for burritos and beachside fish, then enters Valle de Guadalupe to see how Baja wine helped create the modern Baja Med style.

s09e04.description: Tequila country and Guadalajara bring agave, mariachi and Jalisco cooking before Rick reaches Puerto Vallarta, where flamboyant hospitality includes a coffee served literally aflame.

s09e05.description: Mexico City's markets, pulque and surviving Aztec foodways lead to Puebla's talavera pottery and mole, then onward toward Oaxaca and the smoky complexity of mezcal.

s09e06.description: Oaxaca reveals Zapotec traditions, queso Oaxaca and a cuisine rooted in maize and chillies before Rick travels into the lush Chinantla for tropical fruit, vanilla and cacao.

s09e07.description: The final leg reaches Yucatán, where Maya heritage shapes habanero heat, underground pibil cooking, papadzules and sikil pak before the road ends with seafood on the Caribbean coast at Tulum.
